notes: Changed the y-suppression check from "shifted output ends in y" to "original input ends in y". E8 shows "x"→"yy" (orig doesn't end in y, so append even though shifted result "y" ends in y), while "y"→"z" (orig ends in y, suppress). E4's "yy"→"zy" and "ay"→"by" also confirm the check is on the original string's trailing character.
